title: Add sklearn BaseEstimator integration as optional dependency
description:
## Summary

- Integrate with sklearn's `BaseEstimator` and `OutlierMixin` for full compatibility with `Pipeline`, `clone`, `GridSearchCV`, etc.
- Make scikit-learn an **optional** dependency — the core SOS algorithm works with only numpy
- When sklearn is absent, a lightweight `_BaseEstimator` fallback provides `get_params()`, `set_params()`, and `__repr__()`
- Add comprehensive sklearn integration tests (guarded with `importorskip`)
- Bump version to 0.3.0

## Test plan

- [x] All existing tests pass with sklearn installed (48 passed)
- [x] `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `mypy` all clean
- [x] Verified import, fit/predict, get_params/set_params, repr, and CLI all work in a venv without sklearn
- [x] Verified `test_sklearn_integration.py` is skipped when sklearn is absent
- [x] `demo.py` runs successfully

title: Prevent potential infinite loop
description: I've encountered some inputs where `np.isnan(Hdiff)` always returned true, leading to the `predict` call looping forever. Maybe the `tries` check was meant to cover the entire loop?

title: added setup.py (renamed sos to sos.py. sos command is avail. after install)
description:
Hallo Jeroen,

I added a very basic `setup.py` to your projects, which makes available `sos` from the command line and also lets you do things like `from sos import x2d`. The `iris.csv` example file is copied to the same directory that sos is installed to (in my case that is `/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/sos-0.1.0-py2.7.egg/sos/`).

Before adding this to PyPI, the readme probably should be converted to the .rst format.

Groetjes,
Arne

title: Added np.abs before np.sqrt in x2d calculation
description: I noticed that with the upgrade to numpy 1.11 sos started to return 'nan's with the iris dataset across several computers (I tested on MacOSX and Linux systems). The reason is just before of floating point arithmetic leading to a very small negative number in function x2d, just before the np.sqrt is taken. I simply added np.abs just before np.sqrt to protect against this issue.

title: Added the .copy operator to ensure passing by value.
description:
Hi Jeroen Janssens,

I think I have found a bug in the Python implementation. Currently I am working on an implementation in Scala for the Apache Spark platform the scale the algorithm across a large number of clusters. I used the Python script to create unit-tests to verify the workings of the algorithm. I could not find any obvious mistakes, so I did a step by step comparison.

Within Scala the values are assigned as an immutable value which is different as in Python. I found out that this caused a difference in result. To mimic this behavior I added the `.copy()` method on the value which gives a copy. Otherwise, for example `beta[i] == 1`, `betamax == inf` and `Hdiff <= 0`. `betamax` gets assigned as `1`, which is the value of `beta at that moment`, after that the precision of `beta` gets adjusted to `.5`, and then betamax gets also adjusted to `.5`, which does not seem like a correct behavior to me.

``` python
# If not, increase or decrease precision
if Hdiff > 0:
    betamin = beta[i].copy()
    if betamax == np.inf or betamax == -np.inf:
        beta[i] = beta[i] * 2.0
    else:
        beta[i] = (beta[i] + betamax) / 2.0
else:
    betamax = beta[i].copy()
    if betamin == np.inf or betamin == -np.inf:
        beta[i] = beta[i] / 2.0
    else:
        beta[i] = (beta[i] + betamin) / 2.0
```

Before:

``` python
~/Desktop/sos-correct/bin$ < iris.csv ./sos -p 30 | sort -nr | head
0.92552418
0.91794955
0.81657372
0.79410068
0.77251273
0.76652991
0.71135211
0.69634175
0.69305280
0.68967627
```

After the application of the `.copy()`:

``` python
~/Desktop/sos-correct/bin$ < iris.csv ./sos -p 30 | sort -nr | head
0.88569072
0.82241037
0.74932441
0.71168871
0.69498432
0.68975787
0.67562369
0.66990241
0.65935384
0.65740135
```
